Ensure the economic recovery of the host community through enhanced resilient business management capacity of the existing enterprises ( SME) and restarting microenterprises, ensuring at the same time overall social cohesion.

Teknaf Upazila is one of the main host areas for the Rohingya refugees. The most recent influx in 2017 has directly affected the host communities’ food security, economic vulnerability, market access, labour opportunities and environment. The local economy experienced a rising in food, firewood and transport prices, pressure on the water table, basic services, environmental resources and competition for jobs. COVID-19 contributed to adversely affecting the livelihood of the host communities due to the interruption of the supply chain, restriction of movement, closing of businesses and increase in the number of returnee migrant workers. ICCO's long experience of working in the livelihood promotion interventions for the host communities in Teknaf has shown that the main livelihood opportunities that are helping the local economic development are in the areas of horticulture crops, chicken rearing, cattle rearing, dry fish and marine fishery. ICCO Cooperation conducted several studies to identify the gaps of micro-businesses and SMEs operating in these sectors. The study findings show that private sector engagement, proper market linkages along with advanced skill training and financial literacy are required for the business entities for reducing their knowledge gap, enhancing their production and marketing capacity.

Unrestricted transfers can be used entirely as the recipient chooses i.e. there are no restrictions on how the transfer is spent (Definitions of CALP). Conditional cash transfers can include cash for work, cash for assets and cash for training.
